    "id": "dsid_6c3cc0eee4074ee9beb0bc03affeeb32",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/certified-change-control-and-rollback-process-private-deploys-2028.json",
    "title": "Certified Change Control and Rollback Process for Private Deployments",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Certified Change Control and Rollback Process for Private Deployments\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-private-deployments\",\n  \"author\": \"Maya Chen\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"in_review\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2027-11-03\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2028-02-15\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Diego Alvarez\",\n    \"Priya Kapoor\",\n    \"Lina S\\u00f8rensen\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"change-control\",\n    \"rollback\",\n    \"private-deploy\",\n    \"runbook\",\n    \"compliance\",\n    \"slo\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"restricted\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/compliance-anchored-rollback-and-evidence-preservation-playbook-2026\",\n    \"/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/tenant-failure-quarantine-procedures-operator-checklist-2028\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Summary:\\\\n\\\\nThis playbook defines Redwood Inference\\u2019s certified change control and rollback process for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It standardizes classification, approvals, evidence collection, rollback validation, and post-change certification so that field operators and platform engineers can execute changes with predictable risk and auditable artifacts. The goal is to preserve customer SLAs, ensure regulatory evidence capture, and enable reproducible rollbacks when required.\\\\n\\\\nScope:\\\\n\\\\n- Applies to all Private Deployment change categories: control-plane updates, tenant-facing runtime changes (models, quantization, KV/cache migrations), node firmware, GPU firmware or hot-swap operations, and network/topology modifications.\\\\n- Excludes purely documentation edits, UI-only console text, and tenant application deployments managed by the customer.\\\\n\\\\nKey guarantees and SLO impact thresholds:\\\\n\\\\n- Minor changes: expected SLO impact < 1% error-rate delta and < 100 ms median latency delta during a 24-hour window. No mandatory rollback certification.\\\\n- Major changes: expected SLO impact up to 5% error-rate delta or up to 250 ms median latency delta. Require certification before and after change.\\\\n- Critical changes: any change with potential state loss, tenant KV migration, model format migration, or firmware replacement. Must follow the certified rollback procedure and capture full audit bundle.\\\\n\\\\nRoles and responsibilities:\\\\n\\\\n- Change Requester: creates RFC/CAB ticket, provides risk assessment, runbook, and rollback plan. (Usually Platform/Field Eng).\\\\n- Change Approver (CAB): Product/SRE/Compliance representative who signs risk acceptance.\\\\n- Deployment Lead: executes the steps, coordinates oncall, and verifies post-change checks.\\\\n- Rollback Officer: independent verifier who validates that rollback criteria and automation work.\\\\n- Evidence Custodian: owner for bundling logs, artifacts, and signatures for audits. Typically Security/Compliance.\\\\n\\\\nChange classification matrix (quick reference):\\\\n\\\\n1) Routine (low risk)\\\\n   - Examples: config tweaks that do not touch tenant routing, telemetry sampling adjustments.\\\\n   - Approvals: Deployment Lead + 1 peer reviewer.\\\\n   - Evidence: annotated runbook, brief post-change verification note.\\\\n\\\\n2) Major (medium risk)\\\\n   - Examples: model variant rollout, autoscaler policy change, runtime patch with non-destructive KV migration.\\\\n   - Approvals: CAB sign-off required (Product + SRE + Customer Success for high-value tenants).\\\\n   - Evidence: full runbook, telemetry baseline, smoke test results, canary metrics.\\\\n\\\\n3) Critical (high risk)\\\\n   - Examples: stateful migration (KV/Checkpoint relocation), firmware/driver upgrades, hardware replacements requiring node eviction.\\\\n   - Approvals: CAB + Compliance + Customer-notification checklist.\\\\n   - Evidence: complete audit bundle, signed rollback readiness, pre-snapshot artifact.\\\\n\\\\nPre-change checklist (must be attached to RFC):\\\\n\\\\n- Purpose and change window (UTC).\\\\n- Impacted tenants, regions, and model families.\\\\n- SLO impact estimate and rollback criteria (explicit numeric thresholds).\\\\n- Canary plan: sample size, traffic steering, monitoring queries.\\\\n- Backout procedure (step-by-step) with automation commands and manual fallback steps.\\\\n- Snapshot and preservation steps for any stateful component (KV snapshots, model artifacts, node images).\\\\n- Test keys, KMS envelopes, and evidence capture locations (S3 path or secure vault).\\\\n- Communication channels and notification templates (see appendix).\\\\n\\\\nApproval workflow (sequence):\\\\n\\\\n1. Requester fills RFC ticket with attachments: runbook.md, smoke-tests.yaml, pre-change telemetry baseline.\\\\n2. Deployment Lead validates runbook and completes a dry-run with staging dataset if applicable.\\\\n3. CAB reviews within 48 hours for Major/Critical changes. Approval must include explicit SLO acceptance and rollback authorization.\\\\n4. Security/Compliance reviews artifacts for customer-sensitive changes (data residency or evidence capture).\\\\n\\\\nChange window and operational constraints:\\\\n\\\\n- Standard window: 02:00\\u201306:00 UTC for single-region private deploys unless customer chooses otherwise.\\\\n- For cross-region and high-value tenants, schedule rolling windows with at least 24 hours separation between adjacent region changes.\\\\n- Maximum concurrent Major/Critical changes per operator: 1.\\\\n\\\\nCertified rollback procedure (step-by-step):\\\\n\\\\n1. Precondition: Ensure automated rollback scripts are accessible and tested. The automated script must accept the ticket ID and produce a deterministic state target.\\\\n\\\\n2. Freeze traffic: Use routing-control CLI to divert all traffic to warm fallback pool. Example:\\\\n\\\\n   # examples -- routing-control\\\\n   redwood route set --tenant TENANT_A --policy failover --target pool-warm-01 --reason \\\\\\\"rollback-init\\\\\\\" --ticket RFC-1234\\\\n\\\\n3. Snapshot (if not pre-snapshotted):\\\\n\\\\n   - KV: invoke kv-snapshot --tenant TENANT_A --dest s3://redwood-evidence/RFC-1234/kv-snap.json\\\\n   - Models: copy model artifacts with checksum into evidence bucket.\\\\n\\\\n4. Execute automated rollback:\\\\n\\\\n   redwood rollout rollback --ticket RFC-1234 --target stable-tag-2027-10-13 --confirm\\\\n\\\\n5. Verify service convergence: run the post-rollback smoke suite (smoke-tests.yaml) against canary tenants (3 tenants or 1% of traffic, whichever is larger).\\\\n\\\\n6. Independent Rollback Officer validation: the officer must run a scripted verification checklist (listed below) and sign the audit bundle.\\\\n\\\\nRollback verification checklist (to be completed by Rollback Officer):\\\\n\\\\n- Service health: all replicas Ready = true for > 90% of pods in 10-minute window.\\\\n- KV consistency: hash_consistency < 1e-9 between primary and restored copy.\\\\n- Latency: p50/p95 back within pre-change baseline thresholds.\\\\n- Error budget: error-rate less than pre-change baseline + allowable delta.\\\\n- Telemetry anomalies: no new error classes introduced.\\\\n\\\\nEvidence and audit artifacts (bundle requirements):\\\\n\\\\n- RFC ticket and approved CAB sign-off (PDF export).\\\\n- Runbook (final version executed).\\\\n- Automated rollback command logs with stdout/stderr.\\\\n- Telemetry baseline and post-change snapshots (metrics and spans).\\\\n- Node-level logs for any evicted or replaced hardware.\\\\n- Checksums for model/artifact copies.\\\\n- Operator attestations (Deployment Lead and Rollback Officer signed statements).\\\\n\\\\nRetention policy for audit bundles:\\\\n\\\\n- Standard: retain for 2 years for non-regulated customers.\\\\n- Regulated tenants: retain for 7 years or per contract. Stored in encrypted evidence bucket with access controlled by Evidence Custodian.\\\\n\\\\nCommunication and escalation templates (examples):\\\\n\\\\n- Pre-change tenant notification subject: \\\\\\\"Scheduled maintenance: Redwood private deployment change (RFC-1234)\\\\\\\"\\\\n- Post-rollback notification subject: \\\\\\\"Completed rollback: RFC-1234 \\u2014 impact mitigated\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nExample pre-change notification body (short):\\\\n\\\\n   Hello <Customer Team>,\\\\n\\\\n   We will perform scheduled maintenance on <date window> impacting model serving in <region>. Expected impact: brief failover to warm capacity for up to 5 minutes. If you have questions reply to svc-ops@redwood.ai.\\\\n\\\\nCLI and automation snippets (safe examples):\\\\n\\\\n- Run canary traffic shift:\\\\n  redwood route canary --tenant TENANT_A --percent 5 --duration 15m --ticket RFC-1234\\\\n\\\\n- Execute state snapshot (KV):\\\\n  redwood kv snapshot --tenant TENANT_A --dest s3://evidence/RFC-1234/kv.json --encrypt --kms-key arn:aws:kms:region:acct:key/abcd\\\\n\\\\n- Trigger rollback dry-run (no effect):\\\\n  redwood rollout rollback --ticket RFC-1234 --target stable-tag --dry-run\\\\n\\\\nPost-change verification (10-step):\\\\n\\\\n1. Confirm canary latency within baseline.\\\\n2. Check pod readiness and restart counts.\\\\n3. Validate KV checksums.\\\\n4. Run smoke test suite and confirm pass rate >= 99%.\\\\n5. Verify telemetry ingestion (no gaps).\\\\n6. Check for new error traces and classify.\\\\n7. Ensure cost telemetry is within expected bounds (no runaway egress or burst GPU usage).\\\\n8. Validate that KMS envelopes are rotated/untouched as requested.\\\\n9. Confirm customer-facing endpoints respond and model outputs are sanity-checked.\\\\n10. Close the RFC and attach audit bundle.\\\\n\\\\nCertification and sign-off criteria:\\\\n\\\\n- Deployment Lead must attest that the runbook was followed and attach logs.\\\\n- Rollback Officer must confirm rollback tests succeeded (or certify why a manual rollback was required).\\\\n- Compliance must confirm audit bundle completeness for Critical changes.\\\\n- RFC is closed only after all artifacts and sign-offs are in place.\\\\n\\\\nAppendix A \\u2014 Example audit bundle checklist (plain list):\\\\n\\\\n- approval.pdf\\\\n- runbook.md\\\\n- pre-change-metrics.json\\\\n- post-change-metrics.json\\\\n- kv-snap-2028-02-15.json\\\\n- rollback-log-RFC-1234.txt\\\\n- operator-attestation-MayaChen-signed.txt\\\\n\\\\nAppendix B \\u2014 Quick decision tree (text):\\\\n\\\\n- If change touches persistent state -> classify Critical -> require pre-snapshot -> require CAB + Compliance.\\\\n- If automated rollback dry-run fails in staging -> do not schedule for production until fixed.\\\\n- If rollback executes but verification fails -> escalate to oncall SRE and begin coordinated tenant isolation plan.\\\\n\\\\nRelated pages and references:\\\\n\\\\n- Reference: private-deploy-operational-hardening-and-safe-migration-playbook (see migration checklist)\\\\n- Reference: private-deploy-onboarding-and-failover-runbook-2026 (tenant onboarding constraints)\\\\n- SLO definitions: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets (internal link)\\\\n\\\\nDocument revision history:\\\\n\\\\n- 2027-11-03: Draft published by Maya Chen for initial internal review.\\\\n- 2027-12-21: Added automated snapshot examples; updated verification thresholds.\\\\n- 2028-02-15: Strengthened audit bundle requirements and retention policy per Compliance review.\\\\n\\\\nEnd of document.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_6c3cc0eee4074ee9beb0bc03affeeb32\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Certified Change Control and Rollback Process for Private Deployments\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/certified-change-control-and-rollback-process-private-deploys-2028.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-private-deployments\n\ncontent : summary : \\ n \\ nthis playbook defines redwood inference ’ s certified change control and rollback process for private deployments ( vpc and on - prem ). it standardizes classification, approvals, evidence collection, rollback validation, and post - change certification so that field operators and platform engineers can execute changes with predictable risk and auditable artifacts. the goal is to preserve customer slas, ensure regulatory evidence capture, and enable reproducible rollbacks when required. \\ n \\ nscope : \\ n \\ n - applies to all private deployment change categories : control - plane updates, tenant - facing runtime changes ( models, quantization, kv / cache migrations ), node firmware, gpu firmware or hot - swap operations, and network / topology",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Certified Change Control and Rollback Process for Private Deployments\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/certified-change-control-and-rollback-process-private-deploys-2028.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-private-deployments\n\nindependent rollback officer validation : the officer must run a scripted verification checklist ( listed below ) and sign the audit bundle. \\ n \\ nrollback verification checklist ( to be completed by rollback officer ) : \\ n \\ n - service health : all replicas ready = true for > 90 % of pods in 10 - minute window. \\ n - kv consistency : hash _ consistency < 1e - 9 between primary and restored copy. \\ n - latency : p50 / p95 back within pre - change baseline thresholds. \\ n - error budget : error - rate less than pre - change baseline + allowable delta. \\ n - telemetry anomalies : no new error classes introduced. \\ n \\ nevidence and audit artifacts ( bundle requirements )",

{
  "title": "Certified Change Control and Rollback Process for Private Deployments",
  "space": "eng-private-deployments",
  "author": "Maya Chen",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "in_review",
  "created_at": "2027-11-03",
  "last_updated": "2028-02-15",
  "reviewers": [
    "Diego Alvarez",
    "Priya Kapoor",
    "Lina S\u00f8rensen"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "change-control",
    "rollback",
    "private-deploy",
    "runbook",
    "compliance",
    "slo"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "restricted",
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/compliance-anchored-rollback-and-evidence-preservation-playbook-2026",
    "/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/tenant-failure-quarantine-procedures-operator-checklist-2028"
  ],
  "content": "Summary:\\n\\nThis playbook defines Redwood Inference\u2019s certified change control and rollback process for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It standardizes classification, approvals, evidence collection, rollback validation, and post-change certification so that field operators and platform engineers can execute changes with predictable risk and auditable artifacts. The goal is to preserve customer SLAs, ensure regulatory evidence capture, and enable reproducible rollbacks when required.\\n\\nScope:\\n\\n- Applies to all Private Deployment change categories: control-plane updates, tenant-facing runtime changes (models, quantization, KV/cache migrations), node firmware, GPU firmware or hot-swap operations, and network/topology modifications.\\n- Excludes purely documentation edits, UI-only console text, and tenant application deployments managed by the customer.\\n\\nKey guarantees and SLO impact thresholds:\\n\\n- Minor changes: expected SLO impact < 1% error-rate delta and < 100 ms median latency delta during a 24-hour window. No mandatory rollback certification.\\n- Major changes: expected SLO impact up to 5% error-rate delta or up to 250 ms median latency delta. Require certification before and after change.\\n- Critical changes: any change with potential state loss, tenant KV migration, model format migration, or firmware replacement. Must follow the certified rollback procedure and capture full audit bundle.\\n\\nRoles and responsibilities:\\n\\n- Change Requester: creates RFC/CAB ticket, provides risk assessment, runbook, and rollback plan. (Usually Platform/Field Eng).\\n- Change Approver (CAB): Product/SRE/Compliance representative who signs risk acceptance.\\n- Deployment Lead: executes the steps, coordinates oncall, and verifies post-change checks.\\n- Rollback Officer: independent verifier who validates that rollback criteria and automation work.\\n- Evidence Custodian: owner for bundling logs, artifacts, and signatures for audits. Typically Security/Compliance.\\n\\nChange classification matrix (quick reference):\\n\\n1) Routine (low risk)\\n   - Examples: config tweaks that do not touch tenant routing, telemetry sampling adjustments.\\n   - Approvals: Deployment Lead + 1 peer reviewer.\\n   - Evidence: annotated runbook, brief post-change verification note.\\n\\n2) Major (medium risk)\\n   - Examples: model variant rollout, autoscaler policy change, runtime patch with non-destructive KV migration.\\n   - Approvals: CAB sign-off required (Product + SRE + Customer Success for high-value tenants).\\n   - Evidence: full runbook, telemetry baseline, smoke test results, canary metrics.\\n\\n3) Critical (high risk)\\n   - Examples: stateful migration (KV/Checkpoint relocation), firmware/driver upgrades, hardware replacements requiring node eviction.\\n   - Approvals: CAB + Compliance + Customer-notification checklist.\\n   - Evidence: complete audit bundle, signed rollback readiness, pre-snapshot artifact.\\n\\nPre-change checklist (must be attached to RFC):\\n\\n- Purpose and change window (UTC).\\n- Impacted tenants, regions, and model families.\\n- SLO impact estimate and rollback criteria (explicit numeric thresholds).\\n- Canary plan: sample size, traffic steering, monitoring queries.\\n- Backout procedure (step-by-step) with automation commands and manual fallback steps.\\n- Snapshot and preservation steps for any stateful component (KV snapshots, model artifacts, node images).\\n- Test keys, KMS envelopes, and evidence capture locations (S3 path or secure vault).\\n- Communication channels and notification templates (see appendix).\\n\\nApproval workflow (sequence):\\n\\n1. Requester fills RFC ticket with attachments: runbook.md, smoke-tests.yaml, pre-change telemetry baseline.\\n2. Deployment Lead validates runbook and completes a dry-run with staging dataset if applicable.\\n3. CAB reviews within 48 hours for Major/Critical changes. Approval must include explicit SLO acceptance and rollback authorization.\\n4. Security/Compliance reviews artifacts for customer-sensitive changes (data residency or evidence capture).\\n\\nChange window and operational constraints:\\n\\n- Standard window: 02:00\u201306:00 UTC for single-region private deploys unless customer chooses otherwise.\\n- For cross-region and high-value tenants, schedule rolling windows with at least 24 hours separation between adjacent region changes.\\n- Maximum concurrent Major/Critical changes per operator: 1.\\n\\nCertified rollback procedure (step-by-step):\\n\\n1. Precondition: Ensure automated rollback scripts are accessible and tested. The automated script must accept the ticket ID and produce a deterministic state target.\\n\\n2. Freeze traffic: Use routing-control CLI to divert all traffic to warm fallback pool. Example:\\n\\n   # examples -- routing-control\\n   redwood route set --tenant TENANT_A --policy failover --target pool-warm-01 --reason \\\"rollback-init\\\" --ticket RFC-1234\\n\\n3. Snapshot (if not pre-snapshotted):\\n\\n   - KV: invoke kv-snapshot --tenant TENANT_A --dest s3://redwood-evidence/RFC-1234/kv-snap.json\\n   - Models: copy model artifacts with checksum into evidence bucket.\\n\\n4. Execute automated rollback:\\n\\n   redwood rollout rollback --ticket RFC-1234 --target stable-tag-2027-10-13 --confirm\\n\\n5. Verify service convergence: run the post-rollback smoke suite (smoke-tests.yaml) against canary tenants (3 tenants or 1% of traffic, whichever is larger).\\n\\n6. Independent Rollback Officer validation: the officer must run a scripted verification checklist (listed below) and sign the audit bundle.\\n\\nRollback verification checklist (to be completed by Rollback Officer):\\n\\n- Service health: all replicas Ready = true for > 90% of pods in 10-minute window.\\n- KV consistency: hash_consistency < 1e-9 between primary and restored copy.\\n- Latency: p50/p95 back within pre-change baseline thresholds.\\n- Error budget: error-rate less than pre-change baseline + allowable delta.\\n- Telemetry anomalies: no new error classes introduced.\\n\\nEvidence and audit artifacts (bundle requirements):\\n\\n- RFC ticket and approved CAB sign-off (PDF export).\\n- Runbook (final version executed).\\n- Automated rollback command logs with stdout/stderr.\\n- Telemetry baseline and post-change snapshots (metrics and spans).\\n- Node-level logs for any evicted or replaced hardware.\\n- Checksums for model/artifact copies.\\n- Operator attestations (Deployment Lead and Rollback Officer signed statements).\\n\\nRetention policy for audit bundles:\\n\\n- Standard: retain for 2 years for non-regulated customers.\\n- Regulated tenants: retain for 7 years or per contract. Stored in encrypted evidence bucket with access controlled by Evidence Custodian.\\n\\nCommunication and escalation templates (examples):\\n\\n- Pre-change tenant notification subject: \\\"Scheduled maintenance: Redwood private deployment change (RFC-1234)\\\"\\n- Post-rollback notification subject: \\\"Completed rollback: RFC-1234 \u2014 impact mitigated\\\"\\n\\nExample pre-change notification body (short):\\n\\n   Hello <Customer Team>,\\n\\n   We will perform scheduled maintenance on <date window> impacting model serving in <region>. Expected impact: brief failover to warm capacity for up to 5 minutes. If you have questions reply to svc-ops@redwood.ai.\\n\\nCLI and automation snippets (safe examples):\\n\\n- Run canary traffic shift:\\n  redwood route canary --tenant TENANT_A --percent 5 --duration 15m --ticket RFC-1234\\n\\n- Execute state snapshot (KV):\\n  redwood kv snapshot --tenant TENANT_A --dest s3://evidence/RFC-1234/kv.json --encrypt --kms-key arn:aws:kms:region:acct:key/abcd\\n\\n- Trigger rollback dry-run (no effect):\\n  redwood rollout rollback --ticket RFC-1234 --target stable-tag --dry-run\\n\\nPost-change verification (10-step):\\n\\n1. Confirm canary latency within baseline.\\n2. Check pod readiness and restart counts.\\n3. Validate KV checksums.\\n4. Run smoke test suite and confirm pass rate >= 99%.\\n5. Verify telemetry ingestion (no gaps).\\n6. Check for new error traces and classify.\\n7. Ensure cost telemetry is within expected bounds (no runaway egress or burst GPU usage).\\n8. Validate that KMS envelopes are rotated/untouched as requested.\\n9. Confirm customer-facing endpoints respond and model outputs are sanity-checked.\\n10. Close the RFC and attach audit bundle.\\n\\nCertification and sign-off criteria:\\n\\n- Deployment Lead must attest that the runbook was followed and attach logs.\\n- Rollback Officer must confirm rollback tests succeeded (or certify why a manual rollback was required).\\n- Compliance must confirm audit bundle completeness for Critical changes.\\n- RFC is closed only after all artifacts and sign-offs are in place.\\n\\nAppendix A \u2014 Example audit bundle checklist (plain list):\\n\\n- approval.pdf\\n- runbook.md\\n- pre-change-metrics.json\\n- post-change-metrics.json\\n- kv-snap-2028-02-15.json\\n- rollback-log-RFC-1234.txt\\n- operator-attestation-MayaChen-signed.txt\\n\\nAppendix B \u2014 Quick decision tree (text):\\n\\n- If change touches persistent state -> classify Critical -> require pre-snapshot -> require CAB + Compliance.\\n- If automated rollback dry-run fails in staging -> do not schedule for production until fixed.\\n- If rollback executes but verification fails -> escalate to oncall SRE and begin coordinated tenant isolation plan.\\n\\nRelated pages and references:\\n\\n- Reference: private-deploy-operational-hardening-and-safe-migration-playbook (see migration checklist)\\n- Reference: private-deploy-onboarding-and-failover-runbook-2026 (tenant onboarding constraints)\\n- SLO definitions: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets (internal link)\\n\\nDocument revision history:\\n\\n- 2027-11-03: Draft published by Maya Chen for initial internal review.\\n- 2027-12-21: Added automated snapshot examples; updated verification thresholds.\\n- 2028-02-15: Strengthened audit bundle requirements and retention policy per Compliance review.\\n\\nEnd of document.",

    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/private-deployments/network-evidence-mini-ux-and-rollback-lane-prd.json",

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/google_drive",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"network-evidence-mini-ux-and-rollback-lane-prd\",\n  \"owner\": \"Priya Desai\",\n  \"drive_area\": \"shared_drives\",\n  \"path\": \"shared_drives/product/private-deployments\",\n  \"doc_type\": \"doc\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-01-12\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2025-02-03\",\n  \"collaborators\": [\n    \"Marcus Lee\",\n    \"Chen Wu\",\n    \"Ellen Rivera\"\n  ],\n  \"team\": \"product-private-deployments\",\n  \"status\": \"draft\",\n  \"tags\": [\n    \"audit\",\n    \"ux\",\n    \"rollback\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"customer-network\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_artifacts\": [\n    \"CONFLUENCE-PRD-8792\",\n    \"JIRA-PDP-4123\",\n    \"github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/78\"\n  ],\n  \"body\": \"Purpose and context:\\nThis is an early PRD sketch for a compact network evidence handoff UX and a lightweight rollback lane aimed at customer-managed networking within Private deployments. The goal is to reduce on-call friction during network changes while providing minimal, verifiable audit artifacts that satisfy common SOC/infra audits without forcing full heavy-weight evidence bundles for every small change.\\n\\nWhy this exists (problem statement):\\n- Customers running Redwood Private often push small firewall/peering changes that require operator sign-off and produce large audit payloads (costly to store and slow to review).\\n- On-call and operator teams want a quick way to confirm changes and trigger a safe rollback if telemetry shows regressions.\\n- Security/compliance teams want cryptographic continuity (proof-of-change) and a compact searchable index for postmortems.\\n- Current designs create a binary choice: full attestation (heavy) or no evidence (risky). We need a middle path.\\n\\nPrimary goals (MUST):\\n- Define a compact evidence artifact (mini-evidence) that captures the minimal fields needed for verification and forensic replay.\\n- Provide operator UX flows for \\\"approve-with-quick-evidence\\\" and \\\"approve-with-rollback-lane\\\" integrated into the onboarding console and CLI.\\n- Implement sample-based audit retention that keeps full evidence for a fraction of changes and compact artifacts for all.\\n- Ensure artifacts are signed with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or with delegated attestation tokens, depending on deployment mode.\\n\\nSecondary goals (SHOULD):\\n- Developer-friendly API to fetch summarized evidence and reconstruct a timeline for a change window.\\n- First-pass analytics on rollback triggers: detect patterns and provide recommended safety thresholds.\\n- Low-bandwidth option for on-prem customers where evidence upload may be deferred but anchored.\\n\\nUser personas:\\n- Customer Network Operator (CNO): makes and reviews changes. Needs fast sign-off and an easy rollback trigger.\\n- Customer Security Auditor (CSA): needs verifiable chain-of-proof, searchable compact index for investigations.\\n- Redwood SRE/Support: occasionally investigates incidents across customers; needs a consistent minimal artifact shape to triage faster.\\n\\nKey user stories:\\n- As a CNO, I can approve a VPC-peering change with a single signed mini-evidence artifact and a checkbox to create a rollback-lane for 30 minutes.\\n- As a CNO, I can trigger an automated rollback from the console within the defined rollback window; the action emits a rollback evidence artifact.\\n- As a CSA, I can query a compact index (time range + change id) and retrieve a signed summary plus pointers to full evidence if retained.\\n- As Redwood SRE, I can optionally request a full evidence pull for a given change id when investigating anomalies; the request is gated and audited.\\n\\nFunctional requirements (high level):\\n1) Mini-evidence artifact schema (compact):\\n   - change_id (uuid), timestamp (ISO8601), actor (email/orig-system), diff_summary (text, <= 512 chars), risk_score (float 0-1), rollback_token (opaque), signature (base64), evidence_retention_level (enum: full|mini|none), verification_anchor (sha256 digest or KMS reference).\\n   - The schema must be serializable as a newline-delimited JSON for easy streaming.\\n\\n2) Rollback lane primitives:\\n   - When a change is approved with rollback enabled, a rollback_token is issued that can be used to invoke an idempotent rollback API endpoint.\\n   - Rollback tokens expire (configurable, default 30m). Triggering rollback generates a rollback-evidence artifact.\\n   - Rollback endpoints are rate-limited and require both token + operator confirmation for high-risk changes.\\n\\n3) Sampling and retention policy:\\n   - By default keep mini artifacts for all changes for 365 days.\\n   - Sample 1 in N (configurable, default N=20) changes for full evidence retention (payloads, snapshots).\\n   - Allow customer to opt into higher sampling or pin specific change_ids for permanent archival.\\n\\n4) Signing and anchoring:\\n   - Support two modes: customer-KMS signing (preferred for Private) and Redwood-signed attestations for hosted-assist operations.\\n   - All signatures must include a key-id and public key reference stored in the tenant metadata.\\n\\n5) UX/Console flows:\\n   - Approve change modal with: \\\"quick-evidence\\\" summary, toggle: enable rollback (30m/1h/4h), optional free-text justification, and checkbox 'anchor now' to request immediate full evidence capture (may cost extra).\\n   - Timeline view for each change showing mini-evidence, sampled full evidence markers, and rollback actions.\\n\\nNon-functional requirements:\\n- Compact artifacts should be <4KB on average.\\n- Verification path (fetch signature, verify with keyref) should complete in <500ms for UI flows.\\n- Storage overhead must be <5% of current logging pipeline costs assuming default sampling.\\n- Backfill/repair: a mechanism to re-anchor evidence after network failures (deferred upload queue).\\n\\nSuccess metrics (proposed):\\n- Mean time to verify a change (CNO) falls below 2 minutes for 90% of approvals.\\n- Fraction of on-call rollbacks successfully executed within window >= 95% for first 30 days.\\n- Customer satisfaction (NPS/CSAT) on onboarding network changes increases by 15 points for pilot customers.\\n- Audit request fulfillment time for compact index < 1 hour for 95% of requests.\\n\\nImplementation sketch (phases):\\nPhase 0 (spike, 2 wks):\\n- Prototype mini-evidence JSON schema and signature flow using local KMS emulator.\\n- Build minimal console modal mock and CLI knob to test operator flows with a subset of customers.\\n\\nPhase 1 (MVP, 6 wks):\\n- Implement artifact generation, signature plumbing for customer-KMS and Redwood-sign mode.\\n- Basic rollback lane: token issuance, rollback endpoint, and evidence emission.\\n- Sampling engine basic config and retention defaults.\\n- Console UX basic modal + timeline placeholder.\\n\\nPhase 2 (hardening, 8 wks):\\n- Integrate deferred upload queue, storage cost telemetry, and compact index for quick queries.\\n- Add HSM/KMS rotation support and key reference UI.\\n- Implement audit request workflow with RBAC and escalation logging.\\n\\nOpen questions and trade-offs (to resolve):\\n- Do we allow rollback tokens to be exported to customer automation (webhooks/terraform)? Risks: token leakage. Possible mitigation: scoped tokens, IP allowlist, short TTL.\\n- Sampling rate economics: how to balance storage cost vs. investigator time? Need pricing/commit model.\\n- For on-prem air-gapped installs, can we allow offline anchoring with later reconciliation? Design needed for proof-of-origin if time-separated.\\n- How much free-text justification do auditors actually need vs structured fields? Extra fields increase artifact size.\\n\\nSafety and compliance notes:\\n- All consented data fields must honor tenant data retention policy.\\n- Signatures and keys are part of customer security review; include KMS attestability documentation in the final PRD.\\n\\nNext steps (immediate):\\n- Schedule 1hr sync with infra and SRE to validate rollback endpoint constraints (Marcus/Chen/Ellen).\\n- Create spike tickets: PDP-4123 (mini-evidence spike), PDP-4124 (rollback token proto).\\n- Identify two pilot customers (one cloud VPC, one on-prem) and prepare test plan.\\n\\nNotes to self / TODOs (rough):\\n- Draft minimal audit index API (search by actor/change_id/range) and include cost model.\\n- Align with legal on signature acceptability for audits in EU/UK jurisdictions.\\n- Add sample mini-evidence payloads to the Confluence prototyping page.\\n\\nRecent references and links:\\n- see linked artifacts above for the working spike threads.\\n- sketch: github.com/redwood-inference/prototypes/mini-evidence\\n\\nEnd of draft.\\n\\n(Free-form roughness intentionally included \\u2014 looking for product + infra feedback on rollback semantics and sampling economics.)\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_465e8f67162348549c350e62072c564d\"\n}",

{
  "title": "network-evidence-mini-ux-and-rollback-lane-prd",
  "owner": "Priya Desai",
  "drive_area": "shared_drives",
  "path": "shared_drives/product/private-deployments",
  "doc_type": "doc",
  "created_at": "2025-01-12",
  "last_modified": "2025-02-03",
  "collaborators": [
    "Marcus Lee",
    "Chen Wu",
    "Ellen Rivera"
  ],
  "team": "product-private-deployments",
  "status": "draft",
  "tags": [
    "audit",
    "ux",
    "rollback",
    "telemetry",
    "customer-network"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "CONFLUENCE-PRD-8792",
    "JIRA-PDP-4123",
    "github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/78"
  ],
  "body": "Purpose and context:
This is an early PRD sketch for a compact network evidence handoff UX and a lightweight rollback lane aimed at customer-managed networking within Private deployments. The goal is to reduce on-call friction during network changes while providing minimal, verifiable audit artifacts that satisfy common SOC/infra audits without forcing full heavy-weight evidence bundles for every small change.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Customers running Redwood Private often push small firewall/peering changes that require operator sign-off and produce large audit payloads (costly to store and slow to review).
- On-call and operator teams want a quick way to confirm changes and trigger a safe rollback if telemetry shows regressions.
- Security/compliance teams want cryptographic continuity (proof-of-change) and a compact searchable index for postmortems.
- Current designs create a binary choice: full attestation (heavy) or no evidence (risky). We need a middle path.

Primary goals (MUST):
- Define a compact evidence artifact (mini-evidence) that captures the minimal fields needed for verification and forensic replay.
- Provide operator UX flows for "approve-with-quick-evidence" and "approve-with-rollback-lane" integrated into the onboarding console and CLI.
- Implement sample-based audit retention that keeps full evidence for a fraction of changes and compact artifacts for all.
- Ensure artifacts are signed with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or with delegated attestation tokens, depending on deployment mode.

Secondary goals (SHOULD):
- Developer-friendly API to fetch summarized evidence and reconstruct a timeline for a change window.
- First-pass analytics on rollback triggers: detect patterns and provide recommended safety thresholds.
- Low-bandwidth option for on-prem customers where evidence upload may be deferred but anchored.

User personas:
- Customer Network Operator (CNO): makes and reviews changes. Needs fast sign-off and an easy rollback trigger.
- Customer Security Auditor (CSA): needs verifiable chain-of-proof, searchable compact index for investigations.
- Redwood SRE/Support: occasionally investigates incidents across customers; needs a consistent minimal artifact shape to triage faster.

Key user stories:
- As a CNO, I can approve a VPC-peering change with a single signed mini-evidence artifact and a checkbox to create a rollback-lane for 30 minutes.
- As a CNO, I can trigger an automated rollback from the console within the defined rollback window; the action emits a rollback evidence artifact.
- As a CSA, I can query a compact index (time range + change id) and retrieve a signed summary plus pointers to full evidence if retained.
- As Redwood SRE, I can optionally request a full evidence pull for a given change id when investigating anomalies; the request is gated and audited.

Functional requirements (high level):
1) Mini-evidence artifact schema (compact):
   - change_id (uuid), timestamp (ISO8601), actor (email/orig-system), diff_summary (text, <= 512 chars), risk_score (float 0-1), rollback_token (opaque), signature (base64), evidence_retention_level (enum: full|mini|none), verification_anchor (sha256 digest or KMS reference).
   - The schema must be serializable as a newline-delimited JSON for easy streaming.

2) Rollback lane primitives:
   - When a change is approved with rollback enabled, a rollback_token is issued that can be used to invoke an idempotent rollback API endpoint.
   - Rollback tokens expire (configurable, default 30m). Triggering rollback generates a rollback-evidence artifact.
   - Rollback endpoints are rate-limited and require both token + operator confirmation for high-risk changes.

3) Sampling and retention policy:
   - By default keep mini artifacts for all changes for 365 days.
   - Sample 1 in N (configurable, default N=20) changes for full evidence retention (payloads, snapshots).
   - Allow customer to opt into higher sampling or pin specific change_ids for permanent archival.

4) Signing and anchoring:
   - Support two modes: customer-KMS signing (preferred for Private) and Redwood-signed attestations for hosted-assist operations.
   - All signatures must include a key-id and public key reference stored in the tenant metadata.

5) UX/Console flows:
   - Approve change modal with: "quick-evidence" summary, toggle: enable rollback (30m/1h/4h), optional free-text justification, and checkbox 'anchor now' to request immediate full evidence capture (may cost extra).
   - Timeline view for each change showing mini-evidence, sampled full evidence markers, and rollback actions.

Non-functional requirements:
- Compact artifacts should be <4KB on average.
- Verification path (fetch signature, verify with keyref) should complete in <500ms for UI flows.
- Storage overhead must be <5% of current logging pipeline costs assuming default sampling.
- Backfill/repair: a mechanism to re-anchor evidence after network failures (deferred upload queue).

Success metrics (proposed):
- Mean time to verify a change (CNO) falls below 2 minutes for 90% of approvals.
- Fraction of on-call rollbacks successfully executed within window >= 95% for first 30 days.
- Customer satisfaction (NPS/CSAT) on onboarding network changes increases by 15 points for pilot customers.
- Audit request fulfillment time for compact index < 1 hour for 95% of requests.

Implementation sketch (phases):
Phase 0 (spike, 2 wks):
- Prototype mini-evidence JSON schema and signature flow using local KMS emulator.
- Build minimal console modal mock and CLI knob to test operator flows with a subset of customers.

Phase 1 (MVP, 6 wks):
- Implement artifact generation, signature plumbing for customer-KMS and Redwood-sign mode.
- Basic rollback lane: token issuance, rollback endpoint, and evidence emission.
- Sampling engine basic config and retention defaults.
- Console UX basic modal + timeline placeholder.

Phase 2 (hardening, 8 wks):
- Integrate deferred upload queue, storage cost telemetry, and compact index for quick queries.
- Add HSM/KMS rotation support and key reference UI.
- Implement audit request workflow with RBAC and escalation logging.

Open questions and trade-offs (to resolve):
- Do we allow rollback tokens to be exported to customer automation (webhooks/terraform)? Risks: token leakage. Possible mitigation: scoped tokens, IP allowlist, short TTL.
- Sampling rate economics: how to balance storage cost vs. investigator time? Need pricing/commit model.
- For on-prem air-gapped installs, can we allow offline anchoring with later reconciliation? Design needed for proof-of-origin if time-separated.
- How much free-text justification do auditors actually need vs structured fields? Extra fields increase artifact size.

Safety and compliance notes:
- All consented data fields must honor tenant data retention policy.
- Signatures and keys are part of customer security review; include KMS attestability documentation in the final PRD.

Next steps (immediate):
- Schedule 1hr sync with infra and SRE to validate rollback endpoint constraints (Marcus/Chen/Ellen).
- Create spike tickets: PDP-4123 (mini-evidence spike), PDP-4124 (rollback token proto).
- Identify two pilot customers (one cloud VPC, one on-prem) and prepare test plan.

Notes to self / TODOs (rough):
- Draft minimal audit index API (search by actor/change_id/range) and include cost model.
- Align with legal on signature acceptability for audits in EU/UK jurisdictions.
- Add sample mini-evidence payloads to the Confluence prototyping page.

Recent references and links:
- see linked artifacts above for the working spike threads.
- sketch: github.com/redwood-inference/prototypes/mini-evidence

End of draft.

(Free-form roughness intentionally included — looking for product + infra feedback on rollback semantics and sampling economics.)",

  "content_field_names": [
    "body"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_465e8f67162348549c350e62072c564d"
}

This PR introduces a 'tentative swap fuse' that coordinates a deterministic handoff sequence: (1) a rate-limited shadow drain window to warm caches and detect regressions, (2) a tentative (non-committal) swap that labels traffic as active-but-revocable, and (3) a snapshot rollback snapshot + playbook that can be triggered automatically if safety gates fail. The intent is to reduce flakiness during canary -> primary swaps, enable deterministic A/B toggles tied to session affinity, and provide a fast automated rollback path that relies on captured checkpoint snapshots.\",\n  \"commits\": [\n    \"a3b9f7d: introduce tentative swap state machine and API hooks\",\n    \"e7c2b1f: implement rate-limited shadow drain proxy and metrics\",\n    \"c5d4a0b: add snapshot capture and restore utilities (rollback helpers)\",\n    \"f2a1d3e: tests: integration flow for shadow->tentative->commit/rollback\",\n    \"9b4f66c: docs: rollout playbook + operator runbook\"\n  ],\n  \"files_changed\": [\n    \"pkg/rollout/handshake/tentative_swap.go\",\n    \"pkg/rollout/handshake/state_machine_test.go\",\n    \"envoy/filters/traffic_bridge.lua\",\n    \"controller/canary_controller.go\",\n    \"controller/safety_gates.go\",\n    \"deployments/manifests/canary-controller-deployment.yaml\",\n    \"tools/rollback/snapshotter.go\",\n    \"docs/runbooks/rollback-playbook.md\",\n    \"docs/runbooks/tentative-swap-operator.md\",\n    \"tests/integration/seq_handshake_test.go\",\n    \"charts/rollout/values.yaml\",\n    \"pkg/observability/metrics/rollout_metrics.prom\"\n  ],\n  \"review_comments\": [\n    \"Diego Morales (reviewer): Nice decomposition. (2) please add a high-cardinality tag to the 'shadow_drain_success' metric to avoid aggregation confusion.\",\n    \"Maya Patel (author): Added values.yaml entry and made TTL configurable via chart + CRD (defaults to 30s). Also added 'release_id' tag to the metric; refactored metrics export to include release_id and cohort_id.\",\n    \"Anika Shah (reviewer): Integration test is flakey in CI occasionally; observed a deadlock when the snapshot restore fails mid-handshake. {
  "repo": "redwood",
  "pr_number": "531999",
  "title": "Tentative swap fuse with rate-limited shadow drain and snapshot rollback",
  "author": "Maya Patel",
  "created_at": "2026-02-12",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-25",
  "merged_at": "2026-02-25",
  "state": "merged",
  "base_branch": "main",
  "head_branch": "feature/tentative-swap-fuse/shadow-drain-rollback",
  "reviewers": [
    "Diego Morales",
    "Anika Shah",
    "Ravi Kothari"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "rollouts",
    "runtime",
    "safety",
    "tests",
    "docs"
  ],
  "linked_linear": [
    "ENG-2148",
    "ENG-2183"
  ],
  "linked_jira": [
    "SUP-4021"
  ],
  "ci_status": "pass",
  "files_changed_count": "12",
  "additions": "1123",
  "deletions": "439",
  "breaking_change": "false",
  "description": "Motivation: rolling canary handoffs currently observe a small but measurable window where sessions routed to a canary experience partial KV-cache misses and out-of-order prefix replay. This PR introduces a 'tentative swap fuse' that coordinates a deterministic handoff sequence: (1) a rate-limited shadow drain window to warm caches and detect regressions, (2) a tentative (non-committal) swap that labels traffic as active-but-revocable, and (3) a snapshot rollback snapshot + playbook that can be triggered automatically if safety gates fail. The intent is to reduce flakiness during canary -> primary swaps, enable deterministic A/B toggles tied to session affinity, and provide a fast automated rollback path that relies on captured checkpoint snapshots.",
  "commits": [
    "a3b9f7d: introduce tentative swap state machine and API hooks",
    "e7c2b1f: implement rate-limited shadow drain proxy and metrics",
    "c5d4a0b: add snapshot capture and restore utilities (rollback helpers)",
    "f2a1d3e: tests: integration flow for shadow->tentative->commit/rollback",
    "9b4f66c: docs: rollout playbook + operator runbook"
  ],
  "files_changed": [
    "pkg/rollout/handshake/tentative_swap.go",
    "pkg/rollout/handshake/state_machine_test.go",
    "envoy/filters/traffic_bridge.lua",
    "controller/canary_controller.go",
    "controller/safety_gates.go",
    "deployments/manifests/canary-controller-deployment.yaml",
    "tools/rollback/snapshotter.go",
    "docs/runbooks/rollback-playbook.md",
    "docs/runbooks/tentative-swap-operator.md",
    "tests/integration/seq_handshake_test.go",
    "charts/rollout/values.yaml",
    "pkg/observability/metrics/rollout_metrics.prom"
  ],
  "review_comments": [
    "Diego Morales (reviewer): Nice decomposition. Two asks: (1) can we expose the tentative-swap TTL as a per-release config and not hardcode 30s? (2) please add a high-cardinality tag to the 'shadow_drain_success' metric to avoid aggregation confusion.",
    "Maya Patel (author): Added values.yaml entry and made TTL configurable via chart + CRD (defaults to 30s). Also added 'release_id' tag to the metric; refactored metrics export to include release_id and cohort_id.",
    "Anika Shah (reviewer): Integration test is flakey in CI occasionally; observed a deadlock when the snapshot restore fails mid-handshake. Can we make the snapshot restore asynchronous and limit concurrent restores?",
    "Maya Patel (author): Converted restore to a background worker with an in-flight limiter (default 2). Added retry/backoff and stronger assertions in the integration test to avoid timing races.",
    "Ravi Kothari (reviewer): Safety gates look solid but we need an 'operator override' flag documented precisely so SREs know how to force a commit in emergencies. Also, add a circuit-breaker metric when tentative swaps are aborted by rollback.",
    "Maya Patel (author): Added operator_override boolean to CRD and documented fail-open vs fail-closed behaviors in the operator runbook. Added 'tentative_swap_aborts_total' metric and alert suggestion in docs.",
    "Integration CI (comment): integration-tests failed on first run due to flakey ordering in seq_handshake_test.go. Rerun triggered.",
    "CI Bot (comment): integration-tests passed on rerun. All checks green."
  ],
  "ci_checks": [
    "unit-tests: pass",
    "lint: pass",
    "integration-tests: pass (after 1 rerun)",
    "e2e-smoke: pass",
    "security-scan: pass"
  ],
  "merge_outcome": "Merged by squash with commit message: 'tentative swap fuse + rate-limited shadow drain and snapshot rollback; ENG-2148; closes SUP-4021'",
  "release_notes": "Introduce tentative-swap handshake to reduce transient cache misses during canary handoffs; add rate-limited shadow drain to warm caches; add snapshot-based rollback utilities and an operator runbook. Backwards-compatible; rollout opt-in via CRD and chart values.",
  "notes_for_ops": "Operator runbook added at docs/runbooks/rollback-playbook.md. Default behavior is opt-in via chart flag 'rollout.tentativeSwap.enabled=false'. Operators can enable per-environment, tune TTL and concurrency via the CRD fields 'tentativeSwap.ttlSeconds' and 'tentativeSwap.concurrentRestores'. In case of automatic rollback, snapshotter will emit 'rollout.rollback.snapshot_id' tag for forensic playback.",
  "qa_summary": "- Unit tests added for state machine transitions.\n- Integration test simulates shadow drain and tentative commit followed by forced restore path.\n- Manual QA: deployed on canary cluster, exercised A/B fallback by toggling operator_override; verified metrics and rollback-triggered snapshot restores.",
  "manual_migration_steps": "None required. New CRD fields are additive. To opt-in: update chart values and set rollout.tentativeSwap.enabled=true and apply CRD. Existing rollouts unaffected.",
  "associated_incident": "INC-2026-02-canary-flakiness (postmortem referenced in runbook)",
  "changelog_entry": "Feature: tentative swap fuse with shadow drain and snapshot rollback (opt-in) \u2014 adds safer deterministic canary handoffs and fast automated rollback",
  "extra_context": "This PR is part of a small initiative (ENG-2148) to reduce canary-induced customer-facing errors by making handoffs deterministic and observable. Follow-up work: (a) extend tentative swap to multi-region handoffs, (b) add replay harness for snapshot forensic validation.",
  "author_signature": "Maya Patel \u2014 Platform Engineer, rollouts team",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",

    "notes_for_ops",
    "qa_summary"
  ],

}

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_a2e780bb9caf4b06927ba523305c90ae",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-52488-deployment-resilience-lattice-with-compatibility-scoring-and-graceful-throttles.json",
    "title": "Deployment resilience lattice with compatibility scoring and graceful throttles",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-52488\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Deployment resilience lattice with compatibility scoring and graceful throttles\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-20\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-04\",\n  \"creator\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marco Chen\",\n  \"project\": \"deployment-resilience\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W09\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-04-15\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"routing\",\n    \"compatibility-scoring\",\n    \"region-failover\",\n    \"canary\",\n    \"rollback\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.20\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"description\": \"Problem: We need a unified routing and fallback mechanism for model variant rollouts that minimizes customer-visible regressions while maximizing throughput utilization across tiers and regions. Existing heuristics rely on coarse health checks and simple percent-based canaries which don't capture subtle semantic incompatibilities between model variants, nor do they negotiate tiered capacity gracefully during bursts.\\n\\nGoal: Build a 'resilience lattice' \\u2014 an orchestration layer that combines compatibility scoring, topology-aware throttles, and progressive admission control to drive canaries, A/B experiments, shadowing, and auto-rollbacks. The lattice should provide deterministic routing decisions, measurable rollback triggers, and safe degraded modes that preserve latency SLOs when capacity or compatibility falls below thresholds.\",\n  \"rationale\": \"Many production regressions come from semantic drift (model outputs that are syntactically valid but semantically different), uneven regional capacity, and sudden traffic spikes. By making routing decisions based on a multi-dimensional score (compatibility, latency tail, token-cost delta, region proximity) we can preferentially route sensitive traffic to safe variants and fall back to degraded but cost-lower options when needed. This reduces noisy rollbacks and churn for engineers while improving customer continuity.\",\n  \"success_metrics\": [\n    \"Reduce rollback-triggered outages by 50% over next quarter\",\n    \"Decrease mean time to rollback detection from 6m to <90s for semantic regressions\",\n    \"Maintain p99 latency within existing SLOs for >95% of requests during rollouts\",\n    \"Limit percentage of global traffic affected by a single-region failure to <2% via topology-aware rerouting\"\n  ],\n  \"scope\": \"Design and implement the routing layer, compatibility scoring service, admission controller, and CLI/Console controls for rollout policies. Integrate with existing canary telemetry (evals) and Console dashboards. Implement automatic rollback hooks tied to scoring thresholds and quality alerts.\",\n  \"non_goals\": \"We will not modify model training or evaluation tooling in this ticket. Deep semantic evaluation model development (e.g., new eval models) will be handled in a follow-up. This ticket also does not change billing logic or introduce new pricing tiers.\",\n  \"proposal\": \"1) Compatibility scoring microservice that consumes eval snapshots (prompt sets) and runtime signals (per-route n-gram drift, token cost delta, semantic similarity scores) to emit a per-variant compatibility score (0-100).\\n2) Resilience lattice router: a policy engine that combines compatibility score, region proximity, capacity tier, and latency headroom to compute route weights. Supports rules: prefer >=80 score for sensitive routes, degrade to cached prefix variant when score <60, and divert 100% traffic to fallback model if score <40.\\n3) Topology-aware throttles: admission controller that applies soft throttles (graceful reject with 429 hinting, or queueing) instead of hard failures when capacity limits reached; per-customer and global modes.\\n4) Auto-rollback orchestrator: when rolling out, monitor compatibility and latency metrics; if a scoring-policy is violated for N consecutive windows, trigger automated rollback with annotated incident and optional human confirmation for critical customers.\\n5) Console UI: rollout timeline, live compatibility heatmap per region, preflight simulation, and one-click abort/rollback.\\n6) Integrations: connect to KV cache invalidation APIs so fallback to cached prefixes preserves state where feasible.\",\n  \"rollout_plan\": \"Phase 1 (2 sprints): implement scoring service prototype and expose score API; basic routing policy with hard thresholds in non-production.\\nPhase 2 (3 sprints): build lattice router and admission controller; integrate with canary pipeline; add soft-throttle behavior.\\nPhase 3 (2 sprints): Console controls, automated rollback orchestrator, preflight simulation, and runbook.\\nCanary: start with internal-only routes, then trusted customers, then full fleet over 24-72h with progressive weights.\\nFallback test matrix: region failover, tier contention, semantic-drift injection, KV cache cold-start simulation.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Compatibility service returns scores for 100% of variants used in rollouts within 200ms p50 and 1s p95\",\n    \"Routing layer honors policies and falls back to specified variant or cached-prefix mode when score < configured thresholds\",\n    \"Auto-rollback triggers when compatibility < configured threshold for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows and performs rollback in <2m (automated path) or raises alert for manual intervention (controlled path)\",\n    \"Console shows live compatibility heatmap and preflight simulation for any rollout with synthetic traffic option\",\n    \"No customer-visible errors beyond controlled 429s for throttled requests during staged tests\"\n  ],\n  \"risks\": [\n    \"False positives in semantic scoring could cause unnecessary rollbacks \\u2014 mitigate by conservative default thresholds and human-in-the-loop confirmations for high-risk customers\",\n    \"Increased system complexity in router may cause new failure modes; include feature flags and kill-switches\",\n    \"Score compute cost and latency may add overhead \\u2014 plan caching, batching, and async downstream scoring for low-priority routes\",\n    \"Throttling behavior may surface in billing disputes if customers see increased 429s \\u2014 coordinate with CS/pricing team\"\n  ],\n  \"implementation_notes\": \"- Scoring inputs: evaluation suite deltas, fingerprinting (n-gram & embedding drift), p99 latency delta, token-cost multiplier.\\n- Use a sliding window & EWMA to smooth transient spikes.\\n- Router should be implemented as a policy DSL compiled into optimized routing tables; keep hot-path minimal.\\n- Admission controller should expose backpressure hints to SDKs (Retry-After) and be pluggable per-customer.\\n- Persist rollout decisions and rollback reasons in control-plane audit logs for postmortems.\",\n  \"notes_and_links\": [\n    \"Design doc (initial): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEP/Resilience+Lattice+Design\",\n    \"Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1574\",\n    \"Canary telemetry dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/canary-compatibility\",\n    \"Eval prompt set: gs://redwood-evals/resilience-lattice/base_prompts_v2.jsonl\",\n    \"Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Resilience+Lattice+Runbook\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-34107\",\n    \"ENG-46802\",\n    \"ENG-65789\"\n  ],\n  \"parent_issue\": [],\n  \"sub_issues\": [\n    \"ENG-52489\",\n    \"ENG-52490\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-02-21 \\u2014 Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: align on scoring inputs and thresholds. Action items: Marco to prototype score API; Priya to draft Console UX for heatmap.\",\n    \"2025-02-27 \\u2014 Marco Chen: Prototype scoring service up behind feature flag. p50 response ~120ms, p95 ~560ms in test environment. PR created (see links). Need cost estimate for production scale.\",\n    \"2025-03-01 \\u2014 Priya Nair (Product): Reviewed UI flows; asked for ability to pin critical customers to conservative policies. Added as requirement.\",\n    \"2025-03-03 \\u2014 Security review (note): initial threat model reviewed. KMS usage for audit logs recommended. Security to review final design before Phase 2.\",\n    \"2025-03-04 \\u2014 Marco Chen: Added topology-aware throttle prototype. Initial tests show graceful degrade to cached-prefix variant reduces p99 latency spike by ~35% during simulated capacity pressure. Planning integration tests next week.\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"rationale\",\n    \"proposal\",\n    \"rollout_plan\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"risks\",\n    \"implementation_notes\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_a2e780bb9caf4b06927ba523305c90ae\"\n}",
    "kind": "source",

      "assignee": "Marco Chen",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Deployment resilience lattice with compatibility scoring and graceful throttles\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-52488-deployment-resilience-lattice-with-compatibility-scoring-and-graceful-throttles.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: deployment-resilience\nTeam: engineering\n\n##asurable rollback triggers, and safe degraded modes that preserve latency slos when capacity or compatibility falls below thresholds. rationale : many production regressions come from semantic drift ( model outputs that are syntactically valid but semantically different ), uneven regional capacity, and sudden traffic spikes. by making routing decisions based on a multi - dimensional score ( compatibility, latency tail, token - cost delta, region proximity ) we can preferentially route sensitive traffic to safe variants and fall back to degraded but cost - lower options when needed. this reduces noisy rollbacks and churn for engineers while improving customer continuity. # # success metrics",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Deployment resilience lattice with compatibility scoring and graceful throttles\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-52488-deployment-resilience-lattice-with-compatibility-scoring-and-graceful-throttles.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: deployment-resilience\nTeam: engineering\n\nproposal : 1 ) compatibility scoring microservice that consumes eval snapshots ( prompt sets ) and runtime signals ( per - route n - gram drift, token cost delta, semantic similarity scores ) to emit a per - variant compatibility score ( 0 - 100 ). 2 ) resilience lattice router : a policy engine that combines compatibility score, region proximity, capacity tier, and latency headroom to compute route weights. supports rules : prefer > = 80 score for sensitive routes, degrade to cached prefix variant when score < 60, and divert 100 % traffic to fallback model if score < 40. 3 ) topology - aware throttles : admission controller that applies soft throttles ( graceful reject with 429 hinting, or queueing )",

document.title: Deployment resilience lattice with compatibility scoring and graceful throttles
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-52488",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Deployment resilience lattice with compatibility scoring and graceful throttles",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2025-02-20",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-04",
  "creator": "Aisha Patel",
  "assignee": "Marco Chen",
  "project": "deployment-resilience",
  "cycle": "2025-W09",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2025-04-15",
  "labels": [
    "routing",
    "compatibility-scoring",
    "region-failover",
    "canary",
    "rollback"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "release": "runtime-1.20",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "description": "Problem: We need a unified routing and fallback mechanism for model variant rollouts that minimizes customer-visible regressions while maximizing throughput utilization across tiers and regions. Existing heuristics rely on coarse health checks and simple percent-based canaries which don't capture subtle semantic incompatibilities between model variants, nor do they negotiate tiered capacity gracefully during bursts.\n\nGoal: Build a 'resilience lattice' \u2014 an orchestration layer that combines compatibility scoring, topology-aware throttles, and progressive admission control to drive canaries, A/B experiments, shadowing, and auto-rollbacks. The lattice should provide deterministic routing decisions, measurable rollback triggers, and safe degraded modes that preserve latency SLOs when capacity or compatibility falls below thresholds.",
  "rationale": "Many production regressions come from semantic drift (model outputs that are syntactically valid but semantically different), uneven regional capacity, and sudden traffic spikes. By making routing decisions based on a multi-dimensional score (compatibility, latency tail, token-cost delta, region proximity) we can preferentially route sensitive traffic to safe variants and fall back to degraded but cost-lower options when needed. This reduces noisy rollbacks and churn for engineers while improving customer continuity.",
  "success_metrics": [
    "Reduce rollback-triggered outages by 50% over next quarter",
    "Decrease mean time to rollback detection from 6m to <90s for semantic regressions",
    "Maintain p99 latency within existing SLOs for >95% of requests during rollouts",
    "Limit percentage of global traffic affected by a single-region failure to <2% via topology-aware rerouting"
  ],
  "scope": "Design and implement the routing layer, compatibility scoring service, admission controller, and CLI/Console controls for rollout policies. Integrate with existing canary telemetry (evals) and Console dashboards. Implement automatic rollback hooks tied to scoring thresholds and quality alerts.",
  "non_goals": "We will not modify model training or evaluation tooling in this ticket. Deep semantic evaluation model development (e.g., new eval models) will be handled in a follow-up. This ticket also does not change billing logic or introduce new pricing tiers.",
  "proposal": "1) Compatibility scoring microservice that consumes eval snapshots (prompt sets) and runtime signals (per-route n-gram drift, token cost delta, semantic similarity scores) to emit a per-variant compatibility score (0-100).\n2) Resilience lattice router: a policy engine that combines compatibility score, region proximity, capacity tier, and latency headroom to compute route weights. Supports rules: prefer >=80 score for sensitive routes, degrade to cached prefix variant when score <60, and divert 100% traffic to fallback model if score <40.\n3) Topology-aware throttles: admission controller that applies soft throttles (graceful reject with 429 hinting, or queueing) instead of hard failures when capacity limits reached; per-customer and global modes.\n4) Auto-rollback orchestrator: when rolling out, monitor compatibility and latency metrics; if a scoring-policy is violated for N consecutive windows, trigger automated rollback with annotated incident and optional human confirmation for critical customers.\n5) Console UI: rollout timeline, live compatibility heatmap per region, preflight simulation, and one-click abort/rollback.\n6) Integrations: connect to KV cache invalidation APIs so fallback to cached prefixes preserves state where feasible.",
  "rollout_plan": "Phase 1 (2 sprints): implement scoring service prototype and expose score API; basic routing policy with hard thresholds in non-production.\nPhase 2 (3 sprints): build lattice router and admission controller; integrate with canary pipeline; add soft-throttle behavior.\nPhase 3 (2 sprints): Console controls, automated rollback orchestrator, preflight simulation, and runbook.\nCanary: start with internal-only routes, then trusted customers, then full fleet over 24-72h with progressive weights.\nFallback test matrix: region failover, tier contention, semantic-drift injection, KV cache cold-start simulation.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Compatibility service returns scores for 100% of variants used in rollouts within 200ms p50 and 1s p95",
    "Routing layer honors policies and falls back to specified variant or cached-prefix mode when score < configured thresholds",
    "Auto-rollback triggers when compatibility < configured threshold for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows and performs rollback in <2m (automated path) or raises alert for manual intervention (controlled path)",
    "Console shows live compatibility heatmap and preflight simulation for any rollout with synthetic traffic option",
    "No customer-visible errors beyond controlled 429s for throttled requests during staged tests"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "False positives in semantic scoring could cause unnecessary rollbacks \u2014 mitigate by conservative default thresholds and human-in-the-loop confirmations for high-risk customers",
    "Increased system complexity in router may cause new failure modes; include feature flags and kill-switches",
    "Score compute cost and latency may add overhead \u2014 plan caching, batching, and async downstream scoring for low-priority routes",
    "Throttling behavior may surface in billing disputes if customers see increased 429s \u2014 coordinate with CS/pricing team"
  ],
  "implementation_notes": "- Scoring inputs: evaluation suite deltas, fingerprinting (n-gram & embedding drift), p99 latency delta, token-cost multiplier.\n- Use a sliding window & EWMA to smooth transient spikes.\n- Router should be implemented as a policy DSL compiled into optimized routing tables; keep hot-path minimal.\n- Admission controller should expose backpressure hints to SDKs (Retry-After) and be pluggable per-customer.\n- Persist rollout decisions and rollback reasons in control-plane audit logs for postmortems.",
  "notes_and_links": [
    "Design doc (initial): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEP/Resilience+Lattice+Design",
    "Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1574",
    "Canary telemetry dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/canary-compatibility",
    "Eval prompt set: gs://redwood-evals/resilience-lattice/base_prompts_v2.jsonl",
    "Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Resilience+Lattice+Runbook"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-34107",

# Private Deployment Rollback — Fast Lane

Owner: SRE on-call  
Scope: reversible runtime, model, configuration, and routing changes in Redwood Private deployments. Do not use this lane for destructive state migrations, firmware changes, or any rollback whose prior target is not deterministic.

## Contract

Restore the last known-good immutable release snapshot with the smallest safe blast radius. Prefer automated, idempotent rollback. Never roll forward while rollback is in progress.

## Start rollback

Abort expansion and declare an incident when any configured customer SLO or safety gate fires. Unless the deployment contract is stricter, rollback when one of these holds:

- error rate exceeds 1% for 5 minutes;
- p95 latency rises more than 15% from baseline or exceeds the configured absolute ceiling;
- quality evaluation drops more than 0.05;
- a P1 safety/infrastructure signal fires, including corruption, OOM, or sustained severe 5xx errors;
- compatibility remains below its configured threshold for three consecutive one-minute windows.

Ambiguous or under-sampled signals: hold the rollout; do not expand.

## Minimal reversible path

1. Freeze rollout expansion and record incident ID, deployment ID, affected tenant/cohort, current release ID, last-known-good snapshot ID, and trigger.
2. Fence the affected cohort and steer it to the warm fallback pool. Preserve session affinity where supported.
3. Capture a compact pre-rollback record: UTC timestamp, actor, change/incident ID, source and target release IDs, snapshot checksum, trigger metrics, routing diff summary, and signature/key reference. Do not delay rollback to collect raw payloads.
4. Execute the idempotent rollback to the explicit last-known-good snapshot. Never target “latest” or infer a version from wall-clock time.
5. Confirm routing is 100% on the prior version for the affected scope; scale down or quarantine the failed canary.
6. Run smoke checks. Confirm replicas are ready, no new error class exists, error/latency return to baseline bounds, and state checksums match when state is involved.
7. Keep the incident open and escalate to SRE if convergence or smoke checks fail. Do not retry an unknown target.

## Close

Close only after service convergence, a passing smoke suite, and attachment of the compact pre/post evidence to the incident. Schedule forensic replay or bisect from the captured snapshot and deterministic cohort seed where available.

## Evidence basis

- `dsid_7e0acca12c6b40ca851e9fe58d3b21f7`: private-deployment thresholds and forensic snapshot.

# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence Gate

Owner: SRE on-call and Release Engineering  
Scope: Redwood Private deployments, including runtime/model/configuration rollback and stateful or customer-network changes.

## Accepted rollback contract

Rollback is an abort to a deterministic, last-known-good immutable snapshot. Expansion stops before evidence capture or mutation. Critical signals may auto-abort; ambiguous or under-sampled signals auto-hold. Each stage has an explicit owner, evidence record, approval decision, and reconciliation check. No stage may silently fail open.

## Roles

- Incident Commander (IC): owns severity, scope, communications, and exceptions.
- Rollback Operator: executes the reviewed commands.
- Independent Reviewer/Rollback Officer: validates target, evidence, and post-rollback result.
- Customer contact or Compliance: approves when the tenant contract, persistent state, residency, or regulated evidence requires it.

One person may not both execute and independently certify a Major/Critical rollback.

## Trigger and hold gate

Immediately stop expansion and open/attach the incident. Use the customer’s stricter contract when present; otherwise:

- error rate >1% sustained 5 minutes;
- p95 latency >15% above baseline or above the configured absolute ceiling;
- quality evaluation delta worse than -0.05;
- corruption, state-integrity failure, safety violation, node OOM, or sustained severe 5xx/P1 signal;
- compatibility below its configured threshold for three consecutive one-minute windows.

Auto-abort on a critical or integrity signal after minimum samples. Hold—not expand—on an ambiguous, conflicting, or under-sampled signal. IC records the decision.

## Gate 1 — Identify and preserve

1. Record incident/change ID, UTC window, tenant/region/cohort, actor, trigger query and values, current release, deterministic target snapshot, and expected blast radius.
2. Verify the target is immutable, signed/checksummed, compatible with schema/KV/model format, and has an atomic previous pointer or equivalent deterministic reference. Never target “latest.”
3. Fence the affected cohort; preserve session affinity. Divert to a warm fallback if required for safety.
4. Preserve state before mutation when persistent state, KV/cache migration, firmware, or topology is involved.

Evidence: signed compact record containing IDs, timestamps, actor, source/target versions, <=512-character diff summary, risk classification, trigger metric excerpt, snapshot/checksum, routing state, retention class, and verification anchor/key reference. Raw customer payloads are excluded unless consent and policy require them.

## Gate 2 — Approval

- Routine, stateless, pre-authorized auto-abort: IC may authorize execution; independent review may follow immediately after recovery.
- Major/customer-visible: IC plus independent reviewer validates target and command.
- Critical/stateful/network/residency-sensitive: IC, independent reviewer, and required customer/Compliance approver authorize before mutation, unless immediate action is necessary to prevent active harm. Emergency authorization must be recorded and reviewed retrospectively.

Approval names, timestamps, scope, target, and exception rationale become part of the evidence bundle.

## Gate 3 — Staged execution

1. Dry-run target resolution and command rendering when the control plane is available.
2. Roll back the smallest affected cohort/canary with an idempotent command tied to incident/change ID.
3. Verify routing and session fencing, then run smoke tests.
4. If the validation gate passes, expand rollback in controlled stages to the remaining affected scope. If it fails, stop, isolate the tenant/cohort, and escalate; do not loop blindly.
5. Quarantine/scale down the rejected canary only after traffic is confirmed on the previous version.

At every stage capture command result, source/target snapshot, routing weights, readiness, error/latency/quality metrics, and approval to continue.

## Gate 4 — Validation and reconciliation

The independent reviewer confirms:

- desired release and observed release match across control plane, routing layer, nodes, and registry;
- routing is 100% on the intended prior version for the selected scope;
- replicas are ready and restart/error classes are stable;
- error rate, latency, safety, and quality are back within the pre-change/customer baseline;
- state/checksum consistency passes where applicable;
- telemetry has no gap and the compact evidence signature/anchor verifies;
- deferred/offline evidence has reconciled, or an owned incident task with deadline remains open.

A passing smoke suite alone is insufficient when observed state diverges from desired state.

## Closure and retention

Close the rollback only after reconciliation, independent sign-off, customer communication where required, and attachment of the final pre/post bundle. Preserve command logs, trigger evidence, checksums, approvals, verification output, and incident/release links according to tenant retention policy. Schedule deterministic replay/bisect from the snapshot and cohort seed; never expose raw prompts in the compact record.

## Evidence basis

- `dsid_6c3cc0eee4074ee9beb0bc03affeeb32`: classified approvals, deterministic target, snapshots, independent certification, verification, and audit bundle (in review).
- `dsid_7919c26fcfdb43a0b5f95bcb89f94d15`: merged deterministic handoff, bounded restores, snapshot rollback, and forensic snapshot ID.
- `dsid_a2e780bb9caf4b06927ba523305c90ae`: progressive rollout, consecutive-window triggers, human confirmation for critical customers, and auditable decisions.
- `dsid_60d6829368164fca927ac3ee5562a41e`: incident-to-release provenance links for reduced MTTR.
- `dsid_465e8f67162348549c350e62072c564d`: compact signed evidence and deferred reconciliation shape (draft design input only).
